Kustomize

Template-free, per-environment Kubernetes YAML for the Jahez platform — bases, overlays, components, patches and generators, with the same patterns as our Storage, Security and Helm guides. Every output in this guide comes from a real kustomize v5.7.1 build of the repo shown in §2.2.

jahez-prodme-central-1menu-apiorders-dbghcr.io/jahezArgo CD

Part I · High Level

① Foundations — introduction, the need, the solution, comparisons. ② Architecture and workflows — where each part runs, the repo, the build pipeline and one apply end to end. Small snippets only — full files live in Part II.

1

Foundations

1.1Introduction

In one sentence

Kustomize is a Kubernetes-native tool that takes plain, valid YAML and produces a customised copy for each environment by applying patches and transformations declared in a kustomization.yaml file — no templates, no variables, no programming.

Definition

Kustomize is a command-line tool and Go library (sigs.k8s.io/kustomize) maintained by the Kubernetes SIG CLI. You point it at a folder; it reads the folder’s kustomization.yaml, loads the YAML files it lists, applies the changes it declares, and prints one stream of ordinary Kubernetes objects. The same engine is built into kubectl (the -k flag and kubectl kustomize), into Argo CD and into Flux.

The name is “customize” with a K: it customises Kubernetes YAML. The word kustomization means the file (and the folder it describes).

What it is — and what it is not

✓ It is
  • a build tool for YAML: input YAML → output YAML
  • declarative: you describe changes, not steps
  • template-free: every input file is valid Kubernetes YAML you can kubectl apply -f on its own
  • schema-aware: it knows that containers merge by name, that a RoleBinding points at a Role
  • deterministic: same files in → same bytes out (CI and Argo CD agree)
  • works on any kind, CRDs included
✕ It is not
  • a template engine — no {{ }}, no if/loops (that is Helm, Jsonnet, cdk8s)
  • a package manager — no chart versions, repos or dependencies
  • a release tracker — nothing is stored in the cluster, no rollback command
  • a controller — nothing runs inside the cluster
  • a secret store — generated Secrets are only base64

Definitions

①

Kustomization (the file)

A file named kustomization.yaml. It tells Kustomize two things: which YAML files to read and what to change in them.

🎯 Why it exists

Kubernetes YAML has no idea of “dev” or “prod”. This file is the one place where you write “for prod, change X”.

📄 What it looks like
📄 kustomization.yamlyaml
# apps/menu-api/overlays/prod/kustomization.yaml
resources:
  - ../../base          # read these
namespace: jahez-prod   # change this
⚙ What Kustomize does with it

Kustomize opens the folder, reads this file, follows it, and prints the final YAML. The file itself is never sent to the cluster — only the objects it produces.

📍 Where it lives

① git — exactly one per folder: apps/menu-api/base/, apps/menu-api/overlays/prod/…

⚠ Watch out

The name must be exact. If a folder has both kustomization.yaml and kustomization.yml, the build fails.

Deep dive →
②

Resource

Anything you list under resources: — a YAML file, a folder that has its own kustomization.yaml, or a folder in another git repo.

🎯 Why it exists

Kustomize needs a starting point: the objects to load before it changes anything.

📄 What it looks like
📄 overlays/prod/kustomization.yamlyaml
resources:
  - ../../base     # a folder → 7 objects
  - hpa.yaml       # a file   → 1 object
  - pdb.yaml       # a file   → 1 object
⚙ What Kustomize does with it

It loads every item, in order. A folder is built completely first (its own generators and labels), then its objects are added.

Before
nothing loaded
→
After
9 objects in memory
(7 from base + HPA + PDB)
📍 Where it lives

① git — the list is inside kustomization.yaml; the files sit next to it or below it.

⚠ Watch out

A single file outside the folder is blocked: “security; file … is not in or below …”. List the folder instead (../../base).

Deep dive →
③

Base

A folder with the YAML that every environment shares — written once. “Base” is just its role; nothing in the file says “base”.

🎯 Why it exists

Without it you copy the same Deployment, Service and RBAC files into dev, staging and prod — and the copies drift apart (§1.2).

📄 What it looks like
⌘ tree apps/menu-api/basebash
apps/menu-api/base/
├─ kustomization.yaml
├─ service-account.yaml · role.yaml · role-binding.yaml
├─ deployment.yaml · service.yaml · network-policy.yaml
└─ config/appsettings.json
⚙ What Kustomize does with it

Built on its own it gives 7 objects with no namespace, image :latest and 1 replica — deliberately unfinished. Each overlay finishes it.

📍 Where it lives

① git — apps/<service>/base/

⚠ Watch out

Never put environment values in the base (namespace, real image tag, prod CPU). Then every overlay has to undo them.

Deep dive →
④

Overlay

A folder per environment. Its kustomization.yaml includes the base and lists only what is different for that environment.

🎯 Why it exists

The difference between dev and prod becomes a few readable lines instead of being hidden inside 18 copied files.

📄 What it looks like
📄 overlays/dev/kustomization.yamlyaml
# apps/menu-api/overlays/dev/kustomization.yaml
resources:
  - ../../base
namespace: jahez-dev
images:
  - name: ghcr.io/jahez/menu-api
    newTag: dev-4f1c2a9
⚙ What Kustomize does with it

It builds the base first, then applies its own changes on top. Base files are never edited.

Before
base: 7 objects
no namespace · :latest
→
After
dev: same 7 objects
jahez-dev · :dev-4f1c2a9
📍 Where it lives

① git — apps/<service>/overlays/<env>/

⚠ Watch out

An overlay can include another overlay (canary → prod). Keep it to 2–3 levels or nobody can follow it.

Deep dive →
⑤

Patch

A small piece of YAML that changes one specific object — you write only the fields you want to change.

🎯 Why it exists

Prod needs more CPU than dev. Instead of a second Deployment file, you write just the resources part.

📄 What it looks like
📄 deployment-resources-patch.yamlyaml
# overlays/prod/patches/deployment-resources-patch.yaml
apiVersion: apps/v1
kind: Deployment
metadata:
  name: menu-api-deployment     # which object
spec:
  template:
    spec:
      containers:
        - name: menu-api        # which container
          resources:
            requests: {cpu: 500m, memory: 1Gi}
            limits: {memory: 1536Mi}
⚙ What Kustomize does with it

It finds the object by kind + name, then merges your fields into it. Everything you did not mention stays as it was.

Before
cpu 100m · memory 256Mi
probes, ports, mounts
→
After
cpu 500m · memory 1Gi
probes, ports, mounts (kept)
📍 Where it lives

① git — usually overlays/<env>/patches/, listed under patches:

⚠ Watch out

Use the original name (before any prefix). A patch with a target: that matches nothing is silently ignored — always check the output.

Deep dive →
⑥

Transformer

A one-line setting that changes many objects at once: namespace, namePrefix, labels, commonAnnotations, images, replicas.

🎯 Why it exists

Setting the namespace by hand in 11 files is slow and error-prone. One line does it everywhere.

📄 What it looks like
📄 overlays/prod/kustomization.yamlyaml
namespace: jahez-prod
images:
  - name: ghcr.io/jahez/menu-api
    newTag: "2.13.4"
replicas:
  - name: menu-api-deployment
    count: 4
⚙ What Kustomize does with it

It walks every object and stamps the change. It also fixes related fields, e.g. adds namespace to RoleBinding subjects.

Before
11 objects · no namespace
menu-api:latest · 1 replica
→
After
11 objects · jahez-prod
menu-api:2.13.4 · 4 replicas
📍 Where it lives

① git — top-level fields in kustomization.yaml

⚠ Watch out

labels with includeSelectors: true (or old commonLabels) also changes selectors → on a live Deployment the apply fails with “field is immutable”.

Deep dive →
⑦

Generator

Creates a ConfigMap or Secret for you from files or KEY=value lines, and adds a hash of the content to its name.

🎯 Why it exists

When config changes, Pods must restart to read it. A new name (new hash) makes Kubernetes restart them automatically.

📄 What it looks like
📄 base/kustomization.yamlyaml
configMapGenerator:
  - name: menu-api-config-map
    files:
      - config/appsettings.json
⚙ What Kustomize does with it

It builds the ConfigMap, names it with the hash, and rewrites every place that referred to the short name (envFrom, volumes, Role resourceNames).

Before
config/appsettings.json
envFrom: menu-api-config-map
→
After
ConfigMap menu-api-config-map-k8dd95cf8g
envFrom: menu-api-config-map-k8dd95cf8g
📍 Where it lives

① git — inputs in config/ or secrets/; the generator in kustomization.yaml

⚠ Watch out

Generated Secrets are only base64, not encrypted. Never commit real passwords — prod uses ExternalSecret (§6.2).

Deep dive →
⑧

Component

A reusable folder of extra changes (kind: Component) that an overlay can switch on. It does not contain the app — it changes the app.

🎯 Why it exists

Datadog tracing is needed in staging and prod but not dev. Write it once, switch it on where needed.

📄 What it looks like
📄 overlays/staging/kustomization.yamlyaml
# overlays/staging/kustomization.yaml
resources:
  - ../../base
components:
  - ../../../../components/datadog-apm
⚙ What Kustomize does with it

It runs its patches on the objects the overlay already loaded. Dev does not list it, so dev is unchanged.

Before
staging Deployment
env: (none)
→
After
staging Deployment
DD_TRACE_ENABLED=true
DD_LOGS_INJECTION=true
📍 Where it lives

① git — components/<name>/

⚠ Watch out

List it under components:, not resources:. Its apiVersion is kustomize.config.k8s.io/v1alpha1.

Deep dive →
⑨

Replacement

Copies a value from one field into other fields, even in other objects.

🎯 Why it exists

Some values must match across objects, e.g. the image tag should also appear as a version label. Copying by hand drifts.

📄 What it looks like
📄 overlays/canary/kustomization.yamlyaml
replacements:
  - source:
      kind: Deployment
      name: menu-api-deployment
      fieldPath: spec.template.spec.containers.[name=menu-api].image
      options: {delimiter: ":", index: 1}
    targets:
      - select: {kind: Deployment}
        fieldPaths: [spec.template.metadata.labels.[app.kubernetes.io/version]]
        options: {create: true}
⚙ What Kustomize does with it

Late in the build it reads the source value (after images and renames) and writes it into each target field.

Before
image: ghcr.io/jahez/menu-api:2.13.4
labels: app=menu-api
→
After
image: ghcr.io/jahez/menu-api:2.13.4
labels: app=menu-api
        app.kubernetes.io/version=2.13.4
📍 Where it lives

① git — replacements: in kustomization.yaml

⚠ Watch out

The target field must exist unless you set create: true. The old vars: field does the same job but is deprecated.

Deep dive →
⑩

Build

Running Kustomize on a folder to get the final YAML. kubectl apply -k is “build, then send to the cluster”.

🎯 Why it exists

You must see exactly what will reach the cluster — in a PR, in CI, before an apply.

📄 What it looks like
⌘ commandsbash
kustomize build apps/menu-api/overlays/prod     # print only
kubectl apply -k apps/menu-api/overlays/prod     # print + send
⚙ What Kustomize does with it

kustomize build runs everything on your machine and prints. Nothing reaches the cluster until kubectl apply or Argo CD sends it.

Before
folders + kustomization.yaml files
→
After
11 complete objects on stdout
📍 Where it lives

③ your machine / CI — not in git, not in the cluster

⚠ Watch out

kubectl has its own built-in Kustomize, which can be older than the standalone binary → newer fields may fail with “unknown field”.

Deep dive →

1.2Problems or needs

In one sentence

The need: run one service (menu-api) in three environments with small differences. Without a tool you copy YAML per environment and edit the copies; they drift apart and references break.

Step 1 of 3 · Copy per env
  • Where: git repo · Who: you
  • menu-api needs dev, staging and prod. The quick fix: write the 6 files once for dev, then copy them into a folder per environment.
  • 6 objects × 3 envs = 18 files that must stay in sync.
⌘ manual commandsbash
mkdir -p k8s/dev k8s/staging k8s/prod
# write the 6 files for dev, then copy them
cp k8s/dev/*.yaml k8s/staging/
cp k8s/dev/*.yaml k8s/prod/
ls k8s/*/ | wc -l    # 18 files
Step 2 of 3 · Edit by hand
  • Each copy now needs its own namespace, image tag, replica count and resources.
  • People use sed in CI — fragile and invisible in review.
⌘ manual commandsbash
sed -i 's/namespace: .*/namespace: jahez-prod/' k8s/prod/*.yaml
sed -i 's#menu-api:latest#menu-api:2.13.4#' k8s/prod/deployment.yaml
sed -i 's/replicas: 1/replicas: 4/' k8s/prod/deployment.yaml
Step 3 of 3 · Drift
  • Someone adds a readinessProbe to dev only. Prod never gets it.
  • A RoleBinding is renamed in staging but its roleRef is not — the Pod gets 403.
  • Nobody can say what is really different between envs.
⌘ manual commandsbash
diff -r k8s/staging k8s/prod   # hundreds of lines — which ones matter?
⚠ Watch out
Copies drift. The difference between environments is buried inside full files.
→ Next
These three problems are what the solution in §1.3 removes, one by one.

1.3Solution

In one sentence

Write the YAML that every environment shares once, in a base folder. Give each environment a small overlay folder that lists only what is different. kustomize build combines base + overlay into the complete YAML for that environment.

The solution in five steps

  1. One base, written once. apps/menu-api/base/ holds the 6 object files every environment runs (ServiceAccount, Role, RoleBinding, Deployment, Service, NetworkPolicy) plus a config file. It has no namespace, no real image tag and 1 replica — deliberately unfinished.
  2. One overlay per environment. overlays/dev/, overlays/staging/, overlays/prod/. Each contains a kustomization.yaml with only that environment’s differences — dev needs 1 file, prod needs a few more for its extra objects and patches.
  3. The overlay points at the base, it never copies it. The first lines of every overlay are resources: [../../base]. Base files are never edited or duplicated, so a fix in the base reaches every environment.
  4. Differences are typed fields, not text edits. namespace:, images:, replicas:, generators and patches replace the fragile sed commands — Kustomize understands the YAML, so it cannot “miss a match”.
  5. One command builds each environment. kustomize build overlays/prod loads the base, applies the prod changes, renames generated objects and rewires every reference, then prints complete YAML. kubectl apply -k does the same and sends it.

The folder tree

📄 tree jahez-gitops/apps/menu-api (real repo used in this guide)tree
jahez-gitops/apps/menu-api/
├─ base/                ← ① shared, written once
│  ├─ kustomization.yaml
│  ├─ service-account.yaml
│  ├─ role.yaml
│  ├─ role-binding.yaml
│  ├─ deployment.yaml
│  ├─ service.yaml
│  ├─ network-policy.yaml
│  └─ config/
│     └─ appsettings.json
└─ overlays/            ← ② one per environment
   ├─ dev/
   │  └─ kustomization.yaml
   ├─ staging/
   │  └─ kustomization.yaml
   └─ prod/
      ├─ kustomization.yaml
      ├─ hpa.yaml
      ├─ pdb.yaml
      ├─ patches/
      │  ├─ deployment-resources-patch.yaml
      │  └─ deployment-secret-env-patch.yaml
      ├─ config/
      │  └─ appsettings.Production.json
      └─ secrets/
         └─ db.env
jahez-gitops/components/ ← ③ optional extras
├─ datadog-apm/
│  └─ kustomization.yaml
└─ restricted-security/
   └─ kustomization.yaml

What kustomize build does with them — prod

Build each environment

What this overlay adds:

  • namespace jahez-dev
  • image tag dev-4f1c2a9
  • nothing else — base defaults are fine for dev
📄 overlays/dev/kustomization.yamlyaml
apiVersion: kustomize.config.k8s.io/v1beta1
kind: Kustomization

resources:
  - ../../base

namespace: jahez-dev

images:
  - name: ghcr.io/jahez/menu-api
    newTag: dev-4f1c2a9

What this overlay adds:

  • namespace jahez-staging
  • Datadog APM component
  • one config key merged: ASPNETCORE_ENVIRONMENT=Staging
  • tag 2.14.0-rc.1, 2 replicas
📄 overlays/staging/kustomization.yamlyaml
apiVersion: kustomize.config.k8s.io/v1beta1
kind: Kustomization

resources:
  - ../../base

components:
  - ../../../../components/datadog-apm

namespace: jahez-staging

  - name: menu-api-config-map

    newTag: "2.14.0-rc.1"

replicas:

What this overlay adds:

  • namespace jahez-prod, env label, owner annotation
  • Datadog + restricted-security components
  • HPA, PDB and a generated Secret
  • prod config merged, prod CPU/memory, Secret in envFrom, zone spreading
  • tag 2.13.4, 4 replicas
📄 overlays/prod/kustomization.yamlyaml
apiVersion: kustomize.config.k8s.io/v1beta1
kind: Kustomization

# ① What goes in?
resources:
  - ../../base
  - hpa.yaml
  - pdb.yaml
components:
  - ../../../../components/datadog-apm
  - ../../../../components/restricted-security

# ② What should Kustomize generate?
configMapGenerator:
  - name: menu-api-config-map
    behavior: merge
    files:
      - config/appsettings.Production.json
    literals:
      - ASPNETCORE_ENVIRONMENT=Production
secretGenerator:
  - name: menu-api-secret
    envs:
      - secrets/db.env
    type: Opaque

# ③ What changes on every object?
namespace: jahez-prod
labels:
  - pairs:
      jahez.com/env: prod
    includeSelectors: false
    includeTemplates: true
commonAnnotations:
  jahez.com/owner: home-squad

# ④ What changes on specific objects?
images:
  - name: ghcr.io/jahez/menu-api
    newTag: "2.13.4"
replicas:

patches:

How each problem from §1.2 disappears

Problem in §1.2Without KustomizeWith base + overlays
① Copy per env18 copied files to keep in sync8 base files + 1–6 small overlay files; nothing is copied
② Edit by handsed on text — a missed match is silenttyped fields: namespace:, images:, replicas:, patches
③ Drift — probe only in deveach copy changes on its ownadd the probe once in the base → every env gets it on the next build
③ Drift — renamed Role → 403roleRef still points at the old namereferences are rewired automatically (roleRef, subjects, envFrom…)
“What is different in prod?”diff two full foldersread overlays/prod/kustomization.yaml — that is the difference
PR reviewhundreds of changed linesa 1-line change to newTag or a patch file
Baseapps/menu-api/base
Overlaysdev · staging · prod
KindKustomization
Lives ingit — never in the cluster
Outputplain YAML per env
ℹ
Kustomize never edits your base or overlay files and stores nothing in the cluster. It only reads the folders and prints YAML; the cluster just receives normal objects.

1.4Comparisons — Kustomize vs Helm

In one sentence

Helm fills holes in templates; Kustomize edits finished YAML — and you can use both together.

KustomizeHelm
JobProduce env-specific YAML by patching plain YAMLProduce YAML by rendering templates with values
Created & managed bykubernetes-sigs (SIG CLI); built into kubectlCNCF Helm project; separate binary
Typically used byTeams owning their own services (menu-api, orders-db)Vendors publishing installable apps (ingress-nginx, Datadog agent)
Input filesValid Kubernetes YAML + kustomization.yamlChart.yaml, templates/ with Go templates, values.yaml
How you customiseAny field of any object (patch)Only what the chart author exposed in values (or a post-renderer)
Stored in clusterNothing — only the objectsRelease Secret sh.helm.release.v1.<name>.vN per revision
Rollbackgit revert + re-apply (or Argo CD history)helm rollback menu-api 3
Packaging & sharingA git folder or remote URL.tgz chart in a repo or OCI registry
Lifecycle hooks / testsNonepre-install, post-upgrade, helm test
Deletekubectl delete -k (or prune)helm uninstall removes everything it owns
Learning curveLow — it is just YAMLMedium — templates, scoping, tpl, helpers
Jahez choiceOur own microservices, env overlays, Argo CD appsThird-party platform charts — and patched with Kustomize when needed (§6.3)
💡 Tip
Not either/or: helmCharts: lets Kustomize render a chart and then patch it; helm --post-renderer lets Helm hand its output to Kustomize. Both are in §6.3.

When to choose something else

Kustomize for our own services — but use something else for

  • Installing third-party software (ingress-nginx, Datadog agent) → its Helm chart (patch it with Kustomize if needed, §6.3)
  • Real logic — generate 40 tenant namespaces from a list → Helm / Jsonnet / cdk8s
  • Secrets → External Secrets Operator or SOPS, not secretGenerator in git
  • Release history & hooks (migrations before upgrade) → Helm

Kustomization · baseapps/menu-api/base/kustomization.yaml
In one sentence

Lists the 6 shared objects, generates the ConfigMap, stamps app labels.

📄 kustomization.yamlyaml
apiVersion: kustomize.config.k8s.io/v1beta1
kind: Kustomization

# ① What goes in?
resources:
  - service-account.yaml
  - role.yaml
  - role-binding.yaml
  - deployment.yaml
  - service.yaml
  - network-policy.yaml

# ② What should Kustomize generate?
configMapGenerator:
  - name: menu-api-config-map
    files:
      - config/appsettings.json
    literals:
      - ASPNETCORE_ENVIRONMENT=Development

# ③ What changes on every object?
labels:
  - pairs:
      app.kubernetes.io/name: menu-api
      app.kubernetes.io/part-of: jahez-home
    includeSelectors: false
    includeTemplates: true
What each block does
① What goes in?
The six object files. Order does not matter — output is sorted (legacy order: SA, Role, RoleBinding, ConfigMap, Service, Deployment, NetworkPolicy).
② What should Kustomize generate?
One ConfigMap built from appsettings.json plus one literal. It gets a hash suffix; every reference to menu-api-config-map is rewritten.
③ What changes on every object?
Two app labels on metadata and Pod templates, not on selectors (includeSelectors: false) so selectors stay immutable-safe.

Resource · workloadapps/menu-api/base/deployment.yaml
In one sentence

The menu-api Pods: image, ports, config, probes, base resources.

📄 deployment.yamlyaml
apiVersion: apps/v1
kind: Deployment
metadata:
  name: menu-api-deployment
spec:
  replicas: 1
  selector:
    matchLabels:
      app: menu-api
  template:
    metadata:
      labels:
        app: menu-api
    spec:
      serviceAccountName: menu-api-service-account
      containers:
        - name: menu-api
          image: ghcr.io/jahez/menu-api:latest
          ports:
            - name: http
              containerPort: 8080
          envFrom:
            - configMapRef:
                name: menu-api-config-map
          volumeMounts:
            - name: appsettings
              mountPath: /app/config
              readOnly: true
          resources:
            requests:
              cpu: 100m
              memory: 256Mi
            limits:
              memory: 512Mi
          readinessProbe:
            httpGet:
              path: /health/ready
              port: http
      volumes:
        - name: appsettings
          configMap:
            name: menu-api-config-map
What each block does
spec.selector
app: menu-api — immutable after create, so overlays never touch it.
serviceAccountName
Points at menu-api-service-account; Kustomize rewrites it if a prefix is added.
envFrom.configMapRef · volumes.configMap
Both say menu-api-config-map; the build replaces it with the hashed name.
resources
Small base values; prod overrides them with a patch.
image
:latest on purpose — every overlay sets the real tag with images:.

In one sentence

Prod: everything — components, secret, HPA, PDB, patches.

📄 kustomization.yamlyaml
apiVersion: kustomize.config.k8s.io/v1beta1
kind: Kustomization

# ① What goes in?
resources:
  - ../../base
  - hpa.yaml
  - pdb.yaml
components:
  - ../../../../components/datadog-apm
  - ../../../../components/restricted-security

# ② What should Kustomize generate?
configMapGenerator:
  - name: menu-api-config-map
    behavior: merge
    files:
      - config/appsettings.Production.json
    literals:
      - ASPNETCORE_ENVIRONMENT=Production
secretGenerator:
  - name: menu-api-secret
    envs:
      - secrets/db.env
    type: Opaque

# ③ What changes on every object?
namespace: jahez-prod
labels:
  - pairs:
      jahez.com/env: prod
    includeSelectors: false
    includeTemplates: true
commonAnnotations:
  jahez.com/owner: home-squad

# ④ What changes on specific objects?
images:
  - name: ghcr.io/jahez/menu-api
    newTag: "2.13.4"
replicas:
  - name: menu-api-deployment
    count: 4
patches:
  - path: patches/deployment-resources-patch.yaml
  - path: patches/deployment-secret-env-patch.yaml
  - target:
      kind: Deployment
      name: menu-api-deployment
    patch: |-
      - op: add
        path: /spec/template/spec/topologySpreadConstraints
        value:
          - maxSkew: 1
            topologyKey: topology.kubernetes.io/zone
            whenUnsatisfiable: ScheduleAnyway
            labelSelector:
              matchLabels:
                app: menu-api
What each block does
① What goes in?
The whole base, two prod-only objects (HPA, PDB) and two components (Datadog, restricted security).
② What should Kustomize generate?
behavior: merge adds appsettings.Production.json and overrides ASPNETCORE_ENVIRONMENT in the base ConfigMap; a new Secret from secrets/db.env.
③ What changes on every object?
Move everything to jahez-prod, add the env label (templates too) and the owner annotation.
④ What changes on specific objects?
Image tag 2.13.4, 4 replicas, two strategic-merge patch files, and one inline JSON 6902 patch for zone spreading.

5Gi “standard” disk per replica in the base.

📄 stateful-set.yamlyaml
apiVersion: apps/v1
kind: StatefulSet
metadata:
  name: orders-db-stateful-set
spec:
  serviceName: orders-db-service
  replicas: 1
  selector:
    matchLabels:
      app: orders-db
  template:
    metadata:
      labels:
        app: orders-db
    spec:
      containers:
        - name: postgres
          image: postgres:16.4
          envFrom:
            - configMapRef:
                name: orders-db-config-map
          ports:
            - name: postgres
              containerPort: 5432
          volumeMounts:
            - name: data
              mountPath: /var/lib/postgresql/data
  volumeClaimTemplates:
    - metadata:
        name: data
      spec:
        accessModes: ["ReadWriteOnce"]
        storageClassName: standard
        resources:
          requests:
            storage: 5Gi

apiVersion: storage.k8s.io/v1
kind: StorageClass
metadata:
  name: ebs-gp3-encrypted-storage-class
provisioner: ebs.csi.aws.com

allowVolumeExpansion: true
volumeBindingMode: WaitForFirstConsumer
allowedTopologies:
  - matchLabelExpressions:

        values: ["me-central-1a", "me-central-1b", "me-central-1c"]

Patch · JSON 6902apps/orders-db/overlays/prod/patches/stateful-set-storage-patch.yaml
In one sentence

Replaces class + size inside volumeClaimTemplates[0].

📄 stateful-set-storage-patch.yamlyaml
# JSON 6902 patch: list items in volumeClaimTemplates are addressed by index
- op: replace
  path: /spec/volumeClaimTemplates/0/spec/storageClassName
  value: ebs-gp3-encrypted-storage-class
- op: replace
  path: /spec/volumeClaimTemplates/0/spec/resources/requests/storage
  value: 200Gi
What each block does
/spec/volumeClaimTemplates/0/…
Index 0 = the data template. JSON 6902 because strategic merge would replace the whole list.

apiVersion: kustomize.config.k8s.io/v1alpha1
kind: Component

patches:
  - target:
      kind: Deployment
    patch: |-
      apiVersion: apps/v1
      kind: Deployment
      metadata:
        name: any
      spec:
        template:
          metadata:
            labels:
              admission.datadoghq.com/enabled: "true"
            annotations:
              admission.datadoghq.com/dotnet-lib.version: v3.4.1
          spec:
            containers:
              - name: menu-api
                env:
                  - name: DD_TRACE_ENABLED
                    value: "true"
                  - name: DD_LOGS_INJECTION
                    value: "true"
What each block does
kind: Component
Cannot be built alone; runs on the objects of the overlay that lists it.
target: kind: Deployment
Applies to every Deployment of that overlay; the name any in the patch is ignored.

Componentcomponents/restricted-security/kustomization.yaml
In one sentence

Pod Security “restricted” securityContext for every Deployment.

📄 kustomization.yamlyaml
apiVersion: kustomize.config.k8s.io/v1alpha1
kind: Component

patches:
  - target:
      kind: Deployment
    patch: |-
      - op: add
        path: /spec/template/spec/securityContext
        value:
          runAsNonRoot: true
          runAsUser: 10001
          fsGroup: 10001
          seccompProfile:
            type: RuntimeDefault
      - op: add
        path: /spec/template/spec/containers/0/securityContext
        value:
          allowPrivilegeEscalation: false
          readOnlyRootFilesystem: true
          capabilities:
            drop: ["ALL"]
What each block does
op: add …/securityContext
Pod-level: non-root user 10001, RuntimeDefault seccomp.
containers/0/securityContext
Container-level: no escalation, read-only root, drop ALL capabilities.

Kustomization · Helmplatform/redis-cache/kustomization.yaml
In one sentence

Renders the jahez-redis chart then patches it.

📄 kustomization.yamlyaml
apiVersion: kustomize.config.k8s.io/v1beta1
kind: Kustomization

# ① What goes in? — a Helm chart, rendered by `helm template`
helmGlobals:
  chartHome: charts
helmCharts:
  - name: jahez-redis
    releaseName: home-cache
    namespace: jahez-prod
    valuesInline:
      replicas: 2
      maxMemory: 2gb

# ③ What changes on every object?
namespace: jahez-prod
labels:
  - pairs:
      jahez.com/owner: home-squad

# ④ What changes on specific objects? — things the chart does not expose
patches:
  - target:
      kind: Deployment
      name: home-cache-deployment
    patch: |-
      - op: add
        path: /spec/template/spec/nodeSelector
        value:
          jahez.com/pool: memory-optimized
What each block does
① helmGlobals · helmCharts
Runs helm template on the local chart with inline values.
③ namespace · labels
Applied to the chart output like any YAML.
④ patches
Adds a nodeSelector the chart does not expose.

kustomize build --enable-helm platform/redis-cache

2.3Build pipeline — the order never changes

In one sentence

A build starts when someone runs the command (stage 0). Kustomize then runs the same 10 stages in the same order — whatever order you write the fields in. Each stage takes the objects from the previous one, changes them in memory, and passes them on; only stage ⑩ prints.

The pipeline at a glance

Stage by stage — one real run of overlays/prod

We follow one real run of kustomize build apps/menu-api/overlays/prod. Every stage is shown the same way: ① Input → ② Logic → ③ Output. The input is split into RAM — exactly the output of the previous stage — and DISK — only the files this stage newly reads. The logic is overlays/prod/kustomization.yaml growing stage by stage; the lines this stage adds are highlighted. The output lists every object in memory as NEW · CHANGED · UNCHANGED compared with the previous stage. Names are shortened (deployment.yaml = menu-api-deployment); tap any file to see it in full with the changed lines highlighted. Every output is a real build of the prod overlay up to that stage; after stage ⑦ it is byte-for-byte the real prod output.

Step 1 of 11 · run the command
Stage0 of 10Inputyour command + folderOutputparsed kustomization (the plan)
What happens
  • Nothing happens until someone runs the command: you (kustomize build, kubectl apply -k), a CI job, or Argo CD syncing the path.
  • The argument is a folder (or a git URL), not a file. Kustomize looks inside it for exactly one of kustomization.yaml, kustomization.yml or Kustomization.
  • It reads that file and checks apiVersion and kind. Its fields become the plan for stages ① – ⑩ — the order of fields in the file does not matter.
  • Paths inside the file (../../base, hpa.yaml) are relative to this folder, not to where you run the command.
Input → logic → output (tap any file to open it)
① INPUTthe command + the folder you point it at
CMD your terminal / CI / Argo CD
kustomize build apps/menu-api/overlays/prod
# or
kubectl apply -k apps/menu-api/overlays/prod
# or Argo CD sync of path apps/menu-api/overlays/prod
DISK new from disk7 file(s) read in this stage

📁 prod/
📁 patches/
📁 config/
📁 secrets/
② LOGIC · find the entry pointone kustomization file, valid apiVersion + kind
▤ checksout

                       kustomization.yaml

apiVersion: kustomize.config.k8s.io/v1beta1  ✓
kind: Kustomization                          ✓

📌 Remember
Wrong folder → “unable to find one of 'kustomization.yaml', 'kustomization.yml' or 'Kustomization' in directory …” (real error). Run from the repo root, or pass the full path.
Step 2 of 11 · resources
Stage1 of 10Inputthe plan + files on diskOutput9 objects in memory
What happens
  • Kustomize reads resources: from top to bottom.
  • ../../base is a folder with its own kustomization: Kustomize runs the whole pipeline on the base first (its configMapGenerator and labels) and takes the 7 finished objects.
  • hpa.yaml and pdb.yaml are read as-is → 9 objects in memory. Still no namespace, tag :latest, 1 replica.
  • Every object gets an id (group · version · kind · namespace · name). Two objects with the same id → the build stops.

Step 3 of 11 · components
Stage2 of 10Input9 objects + 2 componentsOutputDeployment patched
What happens
  • Each folder under components: runs in order, on the objects already in memory.
  • datadog-apm adds the admission label, the tracer annotation and two DD_* env vars to every Deployment.
  • restricted-security adds Pod and container securityContext (non-root, read-only root, drop ALL).
  • A component adds no copy of the app — it only changes what is there.

Step 4 of 11 · generators
Stage3 of 10Inputobjects + config / secret filesOutputConfigMap re-hashed + new Secret
What happens
  • configMapGenerator with behavior: merge takes the base ConfigMap, adds appsettings.Production.json as a second key and overrides ASPNETCORE_ENVIRONMENT.
  • New content → new hash: the ConfigMap is now menu-api-config-map-k8dd95cf8g. Every reference to it (Deployment envFrom + volume, Role resourceNames) is rewritten to the new name.
  • secretGenerator creates menu-api-secret-t69g58ghht from secrets/db.env.

kind: Kustomization
resources:
  - ../../base

1 new · 3 changed · 6 unchanged
📌 Remember
Never edit a generated ConfigMap in the cluster — the next build replaces it with a new hashed one. Generated Secrets are only base64.
Step 5 of 11 · patches
Stage4 of 10Inputobjects + 2 patch filesOutputDeployment patched 3×
What happens
  • Patches find their target by kind + original name — namespace and prefix are not applied yet.
  • deployment-resources-patch.yaml (strategic merge) sets prod CPU/memory; everything else in the container is kept.
  • deployment-secret-env-patch.yaml replaces the whole envFrom list (no merge key) with the ConfigMap + the new Secret.
  • The inline JSON 6902 patch adds topologySpreadConstraints across zones.

📄 apps/menu-api/overlays/prod/kustomization.yaml+16 lines
apiVersion: kustomize.config.k8s.io/v1beta1
kind: Kustomization
resources:
  - ../../base
  - hpa.yaml
  - pdb.yaml
components:
  - ../../../../components/datadog-apm
  - ../../../../components/restricted-security
configMapGenerator:
  - name: menu-api-config-map
    behavior: merge
    files:
      - config/appsettings.Production.json
    literals:
      - ASPNETCORE_ENVIRONMENT=Production
secretGenerator:
  - name: menu-api-secret
    envs:
      - secrets/db.env
    type: Opaque
patches:
  - path: patches/deployment-resources-patch.yaml
  - path: patches/deployment-secret-env-patch.yaml
  - target:
      kind: Deployment
      name: menu-api-deployment
    patch: |-
      - op: add
        path: /spec/template/spec/topologySpreadConstraints
        value:
          - maxSkew: 1
            topologyKey: topology.kubernetes.io/zone
            whenUnsatisfiable: ScheduleAnyway
            labelSelector:
              matchLabels:
                app: menu-api
③ OUTPUT · RAM in memoryonly the Deployment changed
0 new · 1 changed · 9 unchanged
📌 Remember
A patch with a target: that matches nothing is silently ignored. Lists without a merge key (envFrom, args) are replaced whole.

Stage5 of 10Inputobjects without namespaceOutputevery object in jahez-prod
What happens
  • namespace: jahez-prod is set on every namespaced object.
  • RoleBinding subjects that point at a ServiceAccount get namespace: jahez-prod too.
  • Prod has no namePrefix/nameSuffix, so names stay the same (the canary overlay adds canary-, §4.5).

📌 Remember
An image name with a typo matches nothing — no error, the tag stays :latest. With an HPA, leave replicas to the HPA.
Step 9 of 11 · replacements
Stage8 of 10InputobjectsOutputunchanged — prod has no replacements
What happens
  • Replacements copy a value from one field into other fields (e.g. the image tag into a version label).
  • The prod overlay has no replacements: field, so this stage passes every object through unchanged.
  • The canary overlay uses one (tag → app.kubernetes.io/version) — see §4.5 and §3.15.

0 new · 0 changed · 10 unchanged
📌 Remember
Use replacements for names or values inside strings (env values, args) — Kustomize does not rewrite those on its own.
Step 10 of 11 · fix refs + hash
Stage9 of 10Inputobjects with final namesOutputevery reference consistent
What happens
  • Kustomize keeps a list of name-reference fields: serviceAccountName, envFrom, volumes, roleRef, subjects, Role resourceNames, HPA scaleTargetRef, Ingress backends…
  • Whenever an object got a new name (hash at ③, namespace at ⑤), every reference to it was rewritten. In this prod run that means the hashed ConfigMap and Secret names and the RoleBinding subject namespace.
  • Labels and selectors are not names, so they are never rewritten.

📌 Remember
This is why you always write the short name (menu-api-config-map) in your YAML. A name hidden inside a string is not rewritten — use replacements.
Step 11 of 11 · print
Stage10 of 10Input10 final objectsOutputone YAML stream on stdout
What happens
  • Objects are sorted (default legacy order): ServiceAccount, Role, RoleBinding, ConfigMap, Secret, Service, Deployment… — dependencies first.
  • They are printed as one stream separated by ---.
  • kustomize build stops here. kubectl apply -k sends the stream to the API server; Argo CD compares it with the live cluster (§2.4).

Nothing is sent to the cluster by kustomize build. Exit code 0 does not mean every patch matched — grep the output in CI.

      containers:
        - name: menu-api

          ports:
            - name: http
              containerPort: 8080
          envFrom:
            - configMapRef:
                name: menu-api-config-map
          volumeMounts:
            - name: appsettings
              mountPath: /app/config
              readOnly: true
          resources:
            requests:
              cpu: 100m
              memory: 256Mi
            limits:
              memory: 512Mi
          readinessProbe:
            httpGet:
              path: /health/ready
              port: http
      volumes:
        - name: appsettings
          configMap:
            name: menu-api-config-map

apiVersion: kustomize.config.k8s.io/v1alpha1
kind: Component

patches:
  - target:
      kind: Deployment
    patch: |-
      - op: add
        path: /spec/template/spec/securityContext
        value:
          runAsNonRoot: true
          runAsUser: 10001
          fsGroup: 10001
          seccompProfile:
            type: RuntimeDefault
      - op: add
        path: /spec/template/spec/containers/0/securityContext
        value:
          allowPrivilegeEscalation: false
          readOnlyRootFilesystem: true
          capabilities:
            drop: ["ALL"]

Order facts proved by real builds

Order factWhat it means in practiceProof (real build)
Patches run before namespace / namePrefixA patch target must use the original name and cannot select by the new namespace.Target canary-menu-api-deployment in the same kustomization as namePrefix: canary- → matched nothing, no error.
replicas: runs after patchesIf both set replicas, the replicas: field wins.patch → 7, replicas field → 9 ⇒ output replicas: 9
Name references are fixed at the endroleRef, subjects, serviceAccountName, configMapRef, volumes, HPA scaleTargetRef… follow every rename.prod Role resourceNames became menu-api-config-map-k8dd95cf8g
Each overlay runs its own pipelineThe base is fully built first, then the overlay pipeline runs on its output.prod labels reach HPA/PDB; base labels do not (they were not in the base).

One build, before and after

A snapshot of one build: what you wrote versus what Kustomize printed for the canary overlay.

📄 before · base (what you wrote)yaml
apiVersion: v1
kind: ServiceAccount
metadata:
  name: menu-api-service-account
---
apiVersion: rbac.authorization.k8s.io/v1

  name: menu-api-role-binding

📄 after · kustomize build overlays/canaryyaml
apiVersion: v1
kind: ServiceAccount
metadata:
  labels:
    track: canary
  name: canary-menu-api-service-account
  namespace: jahez-prod
---
apiVersion: rbac.authorization.k8s.io/v1
kind: RoleBinding
metadata:
  labels:
    track: canary
  name: canary-menu-api-role-binding
  namespace: jahez-prod
roleRef:
  apiGroup: rbac.authorization.k8s.io
  kind: Role
  name: canary-menu-api-role
subjects:
- kind: ServiceAccount
  name: canary-menu-api-service-account
  namespace: jahez-prod
FieldChanged byWhy it matters
metadata.namenamePrefix canary-Lets canary and stable live in the same namespace.
metadata.namespacenamespace (from prod overlay)Every namespaced object moves.
roleRef.name, subjects[].namename-reference fixerWithout it the binding points at a Role that does not exist → 403.
subjects[].namespacenamespace transformerServiceAccount subjects need the namespace; Kustomize adds it.
labels.tracklabels transformerLets the canary Service / NetworkPolicy select only canary Pods.

2.4Workflow — how one apply travels from git to running Pods

In one sentence

One command — kubectl apply -k apps/menu-api/overlays/prod — from files in git to running Pods: build on your machine (every stage is in §2.3), send to the API server, then Kubernetes runs it.

Step 1 of 3 · Build
Where③ your machine / CIBlocksstages ⓪ – ⑩ (§2.3)Commandkubectl apply -k apps/menu-api/overlays/prod
  • kubectl apply -k first runs the embedded Kustomize on your machine — exactly the run traced stage by stage in §2.3: load → components → generators → patches → namespace → labels → replicas/images → references → print.
  • Nothing has reached the cluster yet. The result is the same 10 objects kustomize build prints.
💡 Command hint
read overlays/prod→run stages ⓪ – ⑩→YAML in memory→✕ nothing sent yet

The build half of apply -k — identical to kustomize build.

kubectl apply -kbuild first, then send
apps/menu-api/overlays/prodthe folder you point it at
Built objects (tap to open)
③ OUTPUT · RAM in memory10 objects ready to send
Result
10 complete objects in memory, every name and reference final. Step 2 sends them.
Step 2 of 3 · Send
Where④ cluster · API serverBlockskubectlCommandkubectl apply -k apps/menu-api/overlays/prod
  • kubectl takes the printed YAML and sends one apply per object (client-side by default; --server-side for field ownership).
  • API server validates, runs admission (Datadog webhook, Pod Security) and stores in etcd.
💡 Command hint
render→send to API server→create / update objects

The only step that changes the cluster.

kubectl applycreate or update
-k apps/menu-api/overlays/prodrender this kustomization first
▤ example outputout
serviceaccount/menu-api-service-account created
role.rbac.authorization.k8s.io/menu-api-role created
rolebinding.rbac.authorization.k8s.io/menu-api-role-binding created
configmap/menu-api-config-map-k8dd95cf8g created
secret/menu-api-secret-t69g58ghht created
service/menu-api-service created
deployment.apps/menu-api-deployment created
poddisruptionbudget.policy/menu-api-pdb created
horizontalpodautoscaler.autoscaling/menu-api-hpa created
networkpolicy.networking.k8s.io/menu-api-network-policy created
Result
Objects stored. No Kustomize record exists in the cluster — only the objects.
✕ When it fails
Immutable field (selector, volumeClaimTemplates) → the object is rejected; namespace mismatch with -n; missing RBAC for your user → forbidden.
Step 3 of 3 · Run
Where④ cluster · controllersBlocksDeployment · ReplicaSet · scheduler · kubeletCommandkubectl rollout status deploy/menu-api-deployment -n jahez-prod
  • Deployment controller creates a ReplicaSet → 4 Pods; scheduler spreads them over me-central-1a/b/c.
  • kubelet mounts the hashed ConfigMap, injects env from ConfigMap + Secret, starts the container; HPA and PDB start watching.
💡 Command hint
ask API server→watch rollout

Waits until all 4 new Pods are ready.

deploy/menu-api-deploymentkind/name
-n jahez-prodnamespace
▤ example outputout
Waiting for deployment "menu-api-deployment" rollout to finish: 2 of 4 updated replicas are available...
deployment "menu-api-deployment" successfully rolled out
Result

Part II · Low Level

Every field of the Kustomization file, then bases & overlays, components, the Jahez patterns (Storage · Security · Helm · Config · GitOps) and every command. All outputs below are real kustomize v5.7.1 builds.

3

The Kustomization file

① what goes in → ② what to generate → ③ what changes everywhere → ④ what changes on specific objects → ⑤ how values are wired → ⑥ how the build runs.

3.0How a Kustomization works

In one sentence

A Kustomization answers six questions, always in the same order: what goes in, what to generate, what to change everywhere, what to change on specific objects, how to wire values, and how to print.

The file is not a Kubernetes object — the API server never sees it. It is a build recipe that lives in git. Field order in the file does not matter; the pipeline order (§2.3) does.

Question it answersFieldsThink of it as
① What goes in?resources · components · crdsthe ingredients
② What should Kustomize generate?configMapGenerator · secretGenerator · generatorOptions · helmChartsthe printer
③ What changes on every object?namespace · namePrefix · nameSuffix · labels · commonAnnotationsrubber stamps
④ What changes on specific objects?images · replicas · patchessticky notes
⑤ How are values wired?replacementscopy-paste between objects
⑥ How is the build run?sortOptions · buildMetadata · openapi · configurationsprinter settings
Familybuild config
Scopeone folder
Stored in clusternever
Typical useone per base / overlay
📄 apps/menu-api/overlays/prod/kustomization.yaml — every fieldyaml
apiVersion: kustomize.config.k8s.io/v1beta1
kind: Kustomization

# ① What goes in?
resources:
  - ../../base                     # a folder with its own kustomization.yaml
  - hpa.yaml                       # a single file
  - pdb.yaml
  # - https://github.com/jahez/platform-bases//network/default-deny?ref=v1.4.0   # remote git base
components:
  - ../../../../components/datadog-apm
  - ../../../../components/restricted-security

# ② What should Kustomize generate?
configMapGenerator:
  - name: menu-api-config-map
    behavior: merge                # base already has it → merge keys
    files:
      - config/appsettings.Production.json
    literals:
      - ASPNETCORE_ENVIRONMENT=Production
secretGenerator:
  - name: menu-api-secret
    type: Opaque
    envs:
      - secrets/db.env
generatorOptions:
  disableNameSuffixHash: false     # keep the hash → config change = rollout
  labels:
    jahez.com/generated: "true"

# ③ What changes on every object?
namespace: jahez-prod
namePrefix: ""                     # empty = off (canary overlay uses "canary-")
nameSuffix: ""                     # Jahez never uses it: names must end with their kind
labels:
  - pairs:
      jahez.com/env: prod
    includeSelectors: false
    includeTemplates: true
commonAnnotations:
  jahez.com/owner: home-squad

# ④ What changes on specific objects?
images:
  - name: ghcr.io/jahez/menu-api
    newTag: "2.13.4"
replicas:
  - name: menu-api-deployment
    count: 4
patches:
  - path: patches/deployment-resources-patch.yaml        # strategic merge (file)
  - path: patches/deployment-secret-env-patch.yaml
  - target:                                              # JSON 6902 (inline)
      kind: Deployment
      name: menu-api-deployment
    patch: |-
      - op: add
        path: /spec/template/spec/topologySpreadConstraints
        value:
          - maxSkew: 1
            topologyKey: topology.kubernetes.io/zone
            whenUnsatisfiable: ScheduleAnyway
            labelSelector:
              matchLabels:
                app: menu-api

# ⑤ How are values wired between objects?
replacements:
  - source:
      kind: Deployment
      name: menu-api-deployment
      fieldPath: spec.template.spec.containers.[name=menu-api].image
      options:
        delimiter: ":"
        index: 1
    targets:
      - select:
          kind: Deployment
          name: menu-api-deployment
        fieldPaths:
          - spec.template.metadata.labels.[app.kubernetes.io/version]
        options:
          create: true

# ⑥ How is the build run?
sortOptions:
  order: legacy                    # Namespace, CRDs, RBAC… first; Deployments later
buildMetadata:
  - originAnnotations              # stamp config.kubernetes.io/origin on each object
# helmGlobals / helmCharts → render a Helm chart first (needs --enable-helm) · see §6.3

🌳 Every property — open a node for details
• apiVersionstringkustomize.config.k8s.io/v1beta1 (Component: v1alpha1)
• kindstringKustomization · Component
① What goes in?groupthe inputs
resourceslistfiles, folders or git URLs to load

Each entry is a path relative to this folder. A folder must contain its own kustomization.yaml. Order is kept in the output (unless sortOptions says otherwise).

ValueMeaning
hpa.yamlone file, may hold many --- documents
../../basea folder → its kustomization is built first
https://github.com/org/repo//path?ref=v1.4.0a remote git folder pinned to a tag
Deep dive →
componentslistComponent folders to mix in

Run after resources are loaded; each component can generate, patch and transform what is already there.

Deep dive →
crdslistCRD schema files so patches understand custom kinds

Lets strategic merge know list merge keys for CRDs (e.g. Argo Rollouts). Rarely needed.

② What should Kustomize generate?groupnew objects
configMapGeneratorlistbuild ConfigMaps from files / literals / env files
Deep dive →
• namestringrequiredbase name; a -hash is appended
behaviorstringcreate · merge · replace
ValueMeaning
createnew object (error if it exists)
mergeadd/override keys of an inherited one
replacethrow away inherited keys

Default: create

• literalslistKEY=value pairs
• fileslistfile → key named after the file (or key=path)
• envslistenv file → one key per line
• optionsobjectper-generator labels, annotations, disableNameSuffixHash, immutable
secretGeneratorlistsame as above, for Secrets + type
Deep dive →
generatorOptionsobjectdefaults for every generator in this file
Deep dive →
helmCharts · helmGlobalslistrender a chart with helm template
Deep dive →
③ What changes on every object?groupcross-cutting transformers
namespacestringset metadata.namespace on namespaced objects
Deep dive →
namePrefixstringprepend to every name; references follow
Deep dive →
nameSuffixstringappend to every name; references follow

Not used at Jahez: a suffix breaks the rule that names end with their kind.

Deep dive →
labelslistadd labels; choose selectors / templates
Deep dive →
• pairsobjectrequiredthe labels
includeSelectorsbooleanalso selectors (immutable!)

Default: false

includeTemplatesbooleanalso Pod templates

Default: false

• fieldslistcustom field specs for CRDs
commonLabelsobjectdeprecated: labels with includeSelectors: true
Deep dive →
commonAnnotationsobjectadd annotations everywhere (incl. Pod templates)
Deep dive →
④ What changes on specific objects?grouptargeted transformers
imageslistswap name / tag / digest by image name
Deep dive →
replicaslistset replica counts by object name
Deep dive →
patchesliststrategic merge or JSON 6902, from file or inline
Deep dive →
• pathstringpatch file
• patchstringinline patch text
targetobjectselector: group version kind name namespace labelSelector annotationSelector
Deep dive →
• optionsobjectallowNameChange · allowKindChange
⑤ How are values wired between objects?groupcopy fields
replacementslistsource field → target fields
Deep dive →

Deep dive →
⑥ How is the build run?groupoutput & plugins
sortOptionsobjectlegacy (kind order) or fifo (file order)
ValueMeaning
legacyNamespace, CRD, SA, Role… first; webhooks last

buildMetadatalistoriginAnnotations · transformerAnnotations · managedByLabel

• openapiobjectcustom OpenAPI schema for patches
• configurationslistteach transformers new field paths (CRDs)
• generators · transformers · validatorslistKRM function / plugin configs (advanced)
① What goes in?

3.1resources — files, folders, remote git

In one sentence

resources lists everything to load: single files, folders that have their own kustomization, or folders in another git repo.

Question it answersFieldsThink of it as
① Which file or folder?resources[]the shopping list
② Is it local or remote?path · git URL · ?ref=from the shelf or by delivery
③ May it leave this folder?--load-restrictorthe security guard

kind: Kustomization

# ① Which file or folder?

  - hpa.yaml                # one file — may contain several --- documents
  - pdb.yaml

3.3configMapGenerator

In one sentence

configMapGenerator builds a ConfigMap from literals, files and env files, then appends a hash of the content to its name so every change rolls the Pods.

Without the hash, editing a ConfigMap does nothing to running Pods — env vars are read only at start. With the hash, the name changes, Kustomize updates every reference, the Deployment’s Pod template changes and Kubernetes starts a rolling update. Old ConfigMaps stay until pruned.

Question it answersFieldsThink of it as
① What is it called?name · namespacethe label on the box
② Where do the keys come from?literals · files · envs · behaviorwhat goes in the box
③ How is the object stamped?options · generatorOptionsstickers on the box
CreatesConfigMap
Namename + -hash (10 chars)
Change =new name → rollout
Default behaviorcreate
📄 overlays/staging/kustomization.yaml — config generatoryaml
apiVersion: kustomize.config.k8s.io/v1beta1
kind: Kustomization

resources:
  - ../../base

# ① What is it called?
configMapGenerator:
  - name: menu-api-config-map
    # ② Where do the keys come from?   (inherits base keys)
    behavior: merge
    literals:
      - ASPNETCORE_ENVIRONMENT=Staging
      - FEATURE_FLAGS=offers-v2,eta-v3
    files:
      - config/appsettings.Staging.json                 # key = file name
      - appsettings.override.json=config/override.json  # key = left side
    envs:
      - config/feature.env                              # one key per line
    # ③ How is the object stamped?
    options:
      labels:
        jahez.com/config: menu-api
      annotations:
        jahez.com/source: git

📄 overlays/prod/kustomization.yaml — secret generatorsyaml
apiVersion: kustomize.config.k8s.io/v1beta1
kind: Kustomization

resources:
  - ../../base

secretGenerator:
  # ── Opaque: app credentials ──
  - name: menu-api-secret
    type: Opaque
    envs:
      - secrets/db.env
  # ── TLS: certificate for the internal gRPC port ──
  - name: menu-api-tls-secret
    type: kubernetes.io/tls
    files:
      - tls.crt=secrets/tls.crt
      - tls.key=secrets/tls.key
  # ── Registry pull secret ──
  - name: ghcr-pull-secret
    type: kubernetes.io/dockerconfigjson
    files:
      - .dockerconfigjson=secrets/ghcr.json

💡 Tip
Only affects generators in this kustomization — the base’s generator was already built with the base’s options. immutable: true pairs well with the hash: each version is a new object, so it never needs editing, and kubelet stops watching it (less API load).

ReferenceUpdated?
Deployment → serviceAccountName, envFrom, volumes.configMap, secretKeyRef, imagePullSecrets✓
RoleBinding → roleRef.name, subjects[].name✓
Role → resourceNames✓ (when the name matches an object in the build)
HPA / PDB → scaleTargetRef.name✓ HPA; PDB uses a selector, not a name
Service → selector labels✕ labels are not names — use labels with includeSelectors
Ingress → backend.service.name✓
A name inside a string (env value, args, ConfigMap data)✕ use replacements (§3.15)
🛵 At Jahez
Jahez naming rule: every name ends with its kind (-deployment, -role-binding). namePrefix keeps that rule; nameSuffix breaks it (menu-api-deployment-v2). Use prefix or a separate namespace instead.

⚠ Watch out
Because annotations also land in the Pod template, changing one restarts every Deployment. Don’t put build numbers or timestamps here unless a restart is what you want.

Deep dive — the patch directives

📄 overlays/dev/kustomization.yaml — delete thingsyaml
apiVersion: kustomize.config.k8s.io/v1beta1
kind: Kustomization
resources:
  - ../../base
patches:
  # ── delete a field: set it to null ──
  - patch: |-
      apiVersion: apps/v1
      kind: Deployment
      metadata:
        name: menu-api-deployment
      spec:
        template:
          spec:
            containers:
              - name: menu-api
                readinessProbe: null
  # ── delete a list item: $patch: delete ──
  - patch: |-
      apiVersion: apps/v1
      kind: Deployment
      metadata:
        name: menu-api-deployment
      spec:
        template:
          spec:
            volumes:
              - name: appsettings
                $patch: delete
            containers:
              - name: menu-api
                volumeMounts:
                  - name: appsettings
                    $patch: delete
  # ── delete a whole object ──
  - patch: |-
      $patch: delete
      apiVersion: networking.k8s.io/v1
      kind: NetworkPolicy
      metadata:
        name: menu-api-network-policy

3.13patches · JSON 6902

In one sentence

A JSON 6902 patch is a list of operations (add, remove, replace, move, copy, test), each pointing at one exact path — precise where strategic merge is fuzzy.

Question it answersFieldsThink of it as
① Which objects?targetthe address
② What to do?opthe verb
③ Where exactly?path · fromthe JSON Pointer
④ With what?valuethe new content
📄 overlays/dev/kustomization.yaml — JSON 6902 opsyaml
apiVersion: kustomize.config.k8s.io/v1beta1
kind: Kustomization

resources:
  - ../../base

patches:
  - target:
      kind: Deployment
      name: menu-api-deployment
    patch: |-
      # ── add: append to a list with /- ──
      - op: add
        path: /spec/template/spec/containers/0/env
        value: []
      - op: add
        path: /spec/template/spec/containers/0/env/-
        value:
          name: DOTNET_gcServer
          value: "1"
      # ── replace: must already exist ──
      - op: replace
        path: /spec/template/spec/containers/0/ports/0/containerPort
        value: 8081
      # ── test: fail the build if the value is not what we expect ──
      - op: test
        path: /spec/template/spec/serviceAccountName
        value: menu-api-service-account
      # ── keys with / are written ~1, keys with ~ are written ~0 ──
      - op: add
        path: /spec/template/metadata/annotations
        value:
          prometheus.io/scrape: "true"
      - op: replace
        path: /spec/template/metadata/annotations/prometheus.io~1scrape
        value: "false"
      # ── copy and remove ──
      - op: copy
        from: /spec/template/spec/containers/0/resources/requests/memory
        path: /spec/template/spec/containers/0/resources/limits/memory
      - op: remove
        path: /spec/template/spec/containers/0/readinessProbe

3.14patches · target selector & options

In one sentence

target chooses which objects a patch applies to — by group, version, kind, name (regex), namespace, labels or annotations — so one patch can change many objects.

📄 patch targetsyaml
apiVersion: kustomize.config.k8s.io/v1beta1
kind: Kustomization

resources:
  - ../../base
  - ../../../orders-db/overlays/prod

patches:
  # ── every Deployment and StatefulSet (regex on kind) ──
  - target:
      kind: (Deployment|StatefulSet)
    patch: |-
      - op: add
        path: /spec/template/spec/terminationGracePeriodSeconds
        value: 45
  # ── by label selector ──
  - target:
      kind: Deployment
      labelSelector: app.kubernetes.io/part-of=jahez-home
    patch: |-
      - op: add
        path: /spec/revisionHistoryLimit
        value: 5
  # ── by name regex + group/version ──
  - target:
      group: apps
      version: v1
      kind: Deployment
      name: menu-.*
    patch: |-
      - op: add
        path: /spec/minReadySeconds
        value: 10
  # ── rename an object (needs allowNameChange) ──
  - target:
      kind: Service
      name: menu-api-service
    patch: |-
      - op: replace
        path: /metadata/name
        value: menu-api-v2-service
    options:
      allowNameChange: true

⑤ How are values wired?

3.15replacements

In one sentence

replacements copy a value from one field of one object into fields of other objects — the way to put a name or tag inside a string Kustomize would not otherwise touch.

Question it answersFieldsThink of it as
① Where does the value come from?source.kind · source.name · source.fieldPath · source.optionsthe copy
② Where does it go?targets[].select · targets[].reject · targets[].fieldPathsthe paste
③ How is it pasted?options.delimiter · options.index · options.createpaste special
📄 replacements — wire orders-db and the image tag into menu-apiyaml
apiVersion: kustomize.config.k8s.io/v1beta1
kind: Kustomization

resources:
  - ../../base
  - ../../../orders-db/overlays/prod

patches:
  - target:
      kind: Deployment
      name: menu-api-deployment
    patch: |-
      - op: add
        path: /spec/template/spec/containers/0/env
        value:
          - name: ORDERS_DB_HOST
            value: PLACEHOLDER
          - name: APP_VERSION
            value: PLACEHOLDER

# ⑤ How are values wired between objects?
replacements:
  # ── ① source: the Service name of orders-db (after any prefix) ──
  - source:
      kind: Service
      name: orders-db-service
      fieldPath: metadata.name
    # ── ② targets: an env value inside menu-api ──
    targets:
      - select:
          kind: Deployment
          name: menu-api-deployment
        fieldPaths:
          - spec.template.spec.containers.[name=menu-api].env.[name=ORDERS_DB_HOST].value
  # ── image tag → env var + label ──
  - source:
      kind: Deployment
      name: menu-api-deployment
      fieldPath: spec.template.spec.containers.[name=menu-api].image
      options:
        delimiter: ":"
        index: 1
    targets:
      - select:
          kind: Deployment
          name: menu-api-deployment
        fieldPaths:
          - spec.template.spec.containers.[name=menu-api].env.[name=APP_VERSION].value
          - spec.template.metadata.labels.[app.kubernetes.io/version]
        options:
          create: true

images:
  - name: ghcr.io/jahez/menu-api
    newTag: "2.13.4"

3.16helmCharts · helmGlobals

In one sentence

helmCharts runs helm template during the build and feeds the output into the rest of the pipeline, so you can patch a chart like any other YAML.

📄 platform/redis-cache/kustomization.yamlyaml
apiVersion: kustomize.config.k8s.io/v1beta1
kind: Kustomization

# ① What goes in? — a Helm chart, rendered by `helm template`
helmGlobals:
  chartHome: charts
helmCharts:
  - name: jahez-redis
    releaseName: home-cache
    namespace: jahez-prod
    valuesInline:
      replicas: 2
      maxMemory: 2gb

# ③ What changes on every object?
namespace: jahez-prod
labels:
  - pairs:
      jahez.com/owner: home-squad

# ④ What changes on specific objects? — things the chart does not expose
patches:
  - target:
      kind: Deployment
      name: home-cache-deployment
    patch: |-
      - op: add
        path: /spec/template/spec/nodeSelector
        value:
          jahez.com/pool: memory-optimized

4

Bases & overlays

One base per service, one overlay per environment, a stacked overlay for canary.

4.0How layering works

In one sentence

A base holds what every environment shares; each overlay includes the base under resources and adds only what is different; overlays can include other overlays.

Question it answersFieldsThink of it as
① What is shared?base/the printed form
② What differs per env?overlays/<env>/one transparent sheet per env
③ What is optional?components/cartridges you plug in
④ How deep may it stack?resources: ../proda sheet on a sheet — max 2–3
Belongs in the baseBelongs in an overlay
Object kinds every env runs (SA, Role, Deployment, Service, NetworkPolicy)Objects only some envs run (HPA, PDB, StorageClass, ExternalSecret)
Container name, ports, probes, mountsImage tag, replicas, CPU/memory
Labels that never change (app: menu-api)namespace, env labels, owner annotations
Default config (appsettings.json)Env config (appsettings.Production.json) via behavior: merge
💡 Tip
Bases must build on their own — run kustomize build apps/menu-api/base in CI. A base that only works through one overlay is a hidden overlay.

4.1The base — apps/menu-api/base

In one sentence

The menu-api base: six plain objects, one generated ConfigMap and the app labels — no namespace, no tag, one replica.

📄 base/kustomization.yamlyaml
apiVersion: kustomize.config.k8s.io/v1beta1
kind: Kustomization

# ① What goes in?
resources:
  - service-account.yaml
  - role.yaml
  - role-binding.yaml
  - deployment.yaml
  - service.yaml
  - network-policy.yaml

# ② What should Kustomize generate?
configMapGenerator:
  - name: menu-api-config-map
    files:
      - config/appsettings.json
    literals:
      - ASPNETCORE_ENVIRONMENT=Development

# ③ What changes on every object?
labels:
  - pairs:
      app.kubernetes.io/name: menu-api
      app.kubernetes.io/part-of: jahez-home
    includeSelectors: false
    includeTemplates: true

📄 base/deployment.yamlyaml
apiVersion: apps/v1
kind: Deployment
metadata:
  name: menu-api-deployment
spec:
  replicas: 1
  selector:
    matchLabels:
      app: menu-api
  template:
    metadata:
      labels:
        app: menu-api
    spec:
      serviceAccountName: menu-api-service-account
      containers:
        - name: menu-api
          image: ghcr.io/jahez/menu-api:latest
          ports:
            - name: http
              containerPort: 8080
          envFrom:
            - configMapRef:
                name: menu-api-config-map
          volumeMounts:
            - name: appsettings
              mountPath: /app/config
              readOnly: true
          resources:
            requests:
              cpu: 100m
              memory: 256Mi
            limits:
              memory: 512Mi
          readinessProbe:
            httpGet:
              path: /health/ready
              port: http
      volumes:
        - name: appsettings
          configMap:
            name: menu-api-config-map

🛵 At Jahez
The base uses labels with includeSelectors: false on purpose: selectors stay app: menu-api forever, so adding app.kubernetes.io/* labels later never hits the immutable-selector error.

images:
  - name: ghcr.io/jahez/menu-api

replicas:

    count: 2

4.4Overlay · prod

In one sentence

Prod brings everything: both components, a merged ConfigMap, a generated Secret, HPA, PDB, prod resources, zone spreading and owner annotations.

📄 overlays/prod/kustomization.yamlyaml
apiVersion: kustomize.config.k8s.io/v1beta1
kind: Kustomization

# ① What goes in?
resources:
  - ../../base
  - hpa.yaml
  - pdb.yaml
components:
  - ../../../../components/datadog-apm
  - ../../../../components/restricted-security

# ② What should Kustomize generate?
configMapGenerator:
  - name: menu-api-config-map
    behavior: merge
    files:
      - config/appsettings.Production.json
    literals:
      - ASPNETCORE_ENVIRONMENT=Production
secretGenerator:
  - name: menu-api-secret
    envs:
      - secrets/db.env
    type: Opaque

# ③ What changes on every object?
namespace: jahez-prod
labels:
  - pairs:
      jahez.com/env: prod
    includeSelectors: false
    includeTemplates: true
commonAnnotations:
  jahez.com/owner: home-squad

# ④ What changes on specific objects?
images:
  - name: ghcr.io/jahez/menu-api
    newTag: "2.13.4"
replicas:
  - name: menu-api-deployment
    count: 4
patches:
  - path: patches/deployment-resources-patch.yaml
  - path: patches/deployment-secret-env-patch.yaml
  - target:
      kind: Deployment
      name: menu-api-deployment
    patch: |-
      - op: add
        path: /spec/template/spec/topologySpreadConstraints
        value:
          - maxSkew: 1
            topologyKey: topology.kubernetes.io/zone
            whenUnsatisfiable: ScheduleAnyway
            labelSelector:
              matchLabels:
                app: menu-api

✕ When it fails
Changing a label with includeSelectors on the live Deployment → field is immutable. secrets/db.env missing on the CI runner → build error; the PDB blocks node drains if replicas < 3.
📄 overlays/prod/hpa.yamlyaml

  name: menu-api-hpa

    kind: Deployment
    name: menu-api-deployment
  minReplicas: 4
  maxReplicas: 20
  metrics:
    - type: Resource
      resource:
        name: cpu
        target:
          type: Utilization
          averageUtilization: 65

4.5Overlay of an overlay — canary

In one sentence

A canary overlay takes the whole prod overlay as its base, renames everything with canary-, runs one Pod of the new version and drops HPA/PDB.

📄 overlays/canary/kustomization.yamlyaml
apiVersion: kustomize.config.k8s.io/v1beta1
kind: Kustomization

# ① What goes in? — the whole prod overlay
resources:
  - ../prod

# ③ What changes on every object?
namePrefix: canary-
labels:
  - pairs:
      track: canary
    includeSelectors: true      # new objects → safe; canary Pods only

# ④ What changes on specific objects?
images:
  - name: ghcr.io/jahez/menu-api
    newTag: "2.14.0"
replicas:
  - name: menu-api-deployment
    count: 1
patches:
  - target:
      kind: HorizontalPodAutoscaler
    patch: |-
      $patch: delete
      apiVersion: autoscaling/v2
      kind: HorizontalPodAutoscaler
      metadata:
        name: any
  - target:
      kind: PodDisruptionBudget
    patch: |-
      $patch: delete
      apiVersion: policy/v1
      kind: PodDisruptionBudget
      metadata:
        name: any

# ⑤ How are values wired?
replacements:
  - source:
      kind: Deployment
      name: menu-api-deployment
      fieldPath: spec.template.spec.containers.[name=menu-api].image
      options:
        delimiter: ":"
        index: 1
    targets:
      - select:
          kind: Deployment
        fieldPaths:
          - spec.template.metadata.labels.[app.kubernetes.io/version]
        options:
          create: true

5

Components

Reusable, opt-in bundles of changes.

5.0How a Component works

In one sentence

A Component is a kustomization with kind: Component that is not built alone: an overlay lists it under components: and it runs its patches, generators and resources on the overlay’s objects.

Question it answersFieldsThink of it as
① What is it?apiVersion: …/v1alpha1 · kind: Componenta plug-in cartridge
② Who switches it on?components: in an overlaythe env that wants it
③ What can it do?resources · patches · generators · labels…anything a kustomization can
BaseOverlayComponent
kindKustomizationKustomizationComponent (v1alpha1)
Builds alone?yesyesno — needs a parent
Listed underresources—components
Sees the parent’s objects?noyes (its own resources)yes — it patches them
Use forshared appone environmentan optional feature used by some envs
Jahez examplesapps/menu-api/baseoverlays/proddatadog-apm · restricted-security
ℹ
Why not a base? Two overlays that both include a “datadog base” would load menu-api twice → “already registered id”. A Component adds no copy; it only changes what is already there.

5.1Component · datadog-apm

In one sentence

datadog-apm turns on Datadog’s admission-controller injection and trace env vars for every Deployment in the env that opts in.

📄 components/datadog-apm/kustomization.yamlyaml
apiVersion: kustomize.config.k8s.io/v1alpha1
kind: Component

patches:
  - target:
      kind: Deployment
    patch: |-
      apiVersion: apps/v1
      kind: Deployment
      metadata:
        name: any
      spec:
        template:
          metadata:
            labels:
              admission.datadoghq.com/enabled: "true"
            annotations:
              admission.datadoghq.com/dotnet-lib.version: v3.4.1
          spec:
            containers:
              - name: menu-api
                env:
                  - name: DD_TRACE_ENABLED
                    value: "true"
                  - name: DD_LOGS_INJECTION
                    value: "true"

🪤 Exam trap
The patch names the container menu-api. On a service whose container has another name, strategic merge adds a second, image-less container and the apply fails. For a truly shared component, use a JSON 6902 op on containers/0, or name every main container app.

5.2Component · restricted-security

In one sentence

restricted-security applies the Pod Security “restricted” profile — non-root, no privilege escalation, read-only root, all capabilities dropped, RuntimeDefault seccomp.

📄 components/restricted-security/kustomization.yamlyaml
apiVersion: kustomize.config.k8s.io/v1alpha1
kind: Component

patches:
  - target:
      kind: Deployment
    patch: |-
      - op: add
        path: /spec/template/spec/securityContext
        value:
          runAsNonRoot: true
          runAsUser: 10001
          fsGroup: 10001
          seccompProfile:
            type: RuntimeDefault
      - op: add
        path: /spec/template/spec/containers/0/securityContext
        value:
          allowPrivilegeEscalation: false
          readOnlyRootFilesystem: true
          capabilities:
            drop: ["ALL"]

5.3Opt-in matrix

In one sentence

Which environment opts into which component — and the order they run in.

Componentdevstagingprodcanary
datadog-apm—✓✓✓ (via prod)

ℹ
Components run in the order listed, after the overlay’s resources load and before the overlay’s own patches and transformers. A later component sees the earlier one’s changes.

6.1Storage — one StatefulSet, a different disk per env

In one sentence

orders-db keeps one StatefulSet in the base and lets each overlay choose the disk: class, size and replica count — the Storage guide’s objects, varied per env with one JSON 6902 patch.

Question it answersFieldsThink of it as
① What is the disk?volumeClaimTemplates[0].spec.resources.requests.storage · accessModessize of the box
② Where is it really?storageClassName · StorageClass (cluster-scoped)which warehouse
③ How many?replicasone box per replica
④ What happens at the end?reclaimPolicy: Retainkeep the box after delete

Lifecycle — create → grow → change class

Step 1 of 3 · Create
  • Where: cluster · Who: you (apply) → StatefulSet controller → EBS CSI
  • StatefulSet creates PVC data-orders-db-stateful-set-0..2 from the template.
  • WaitForFirstConsumer: each disk is created in the zone of its Pod.
⌘ commandsbash
kubectl apply -k apps/orders-db/overlays/prod
kubectl get pvc -n jahez-prod -l app=orders-db
▤ Outputout
NAME                              STATUS   CAPACITY   STORAGECLASS
data-orders-db-stateful-set-0     Bound    200Gi      ebs-gp3-encrypted-storage-class
data-orders-db-stateful-set-1     Bound    200Gi      ebs-gp3-encrypted-storage-class
data-orders-db-stateful-set-2     Bound    200Gi      ebs-gp3-encrypted-storage-class
Step 2 of 3 · Grow 200→300Gi
  • Trap: changing the template size in the overlay and applying fails — volumeClaimTemplates are immutable.
  • Do it in two moves: patch each live PVC (class allows expansion), then update the overlay so new replicas match.
▤ kubectl apply -k after editing the patch to 300Giout
The StatefulSet "orders-db-stateful-set" is invalid: spec: Forbidden: updates to statefulset spec for fields other than 'replicas', 'ordinals', 'template', 'updateStrategy', 'persistentVolumeClaimRetentionPolicy' and 'minReadySeconds' are forbidden
⌘ the safe waybash
for i in 0 1 2; do
  kubectl patch pvc data-orders-db-stateful-set-$i -n jahez-prod \
    -p '{"spec":{"resources":{"requests":{"storage":"300Gi"}}}}'
done
# then recreate the StatefulSet object only — Pods and PVCs stay
kubectl delete sts orders-db-stateful-set -n jahez-prod --cascade=orphan
kubectl apply -k apps/orders-db/overlays/prod
Step 3 of 3 · Change class
  • A PVC’s storageClassName can never change. New class = new disks = data migration (pg_dump / logical replication / Velero).
  • Kustomize makes the YAML change trivial; the data move is the real work.
⚠ Watch out
Prod overlay must also keep reclaimPolicy: Retain so a mistaken kubectl delete -k never deletes the EBS volumes.
🛵 At Jahez
The StorageClass is cluster-scoped: namespace: jahez-prod did not touch it (real output above). Keep cluster-scoped objects in a platform folder applied once, not inside every app — otherwise two apps fight over it.

6.2Security — RBAC, Pod security, NetworkPolicy, Secrets

In one sentence

The Security guide’s objects — ServiceAccount, Role, RoleBinding, NetworkPolicy, securityContext, Secrets — stay correct per env because Kustomize rewrites every reference when names or namespaces change.

Security objectWhat Kustomize does for youWhat you must still do
ServiceAccountprefix + namespace; Deployment serviceAccountName followskeep automountServiceAccountToken: false unless the app calls the API
Role / ClusterRoleresourceNames follow hashed ConfigMap/Secret names (real: menu-api-config-map-k8dd95cf8g)review verbs — Kustomize never narrows them
RoleBindingroleRef, subjects[].name and subjects[].namespace rewrittenClusterRoleBinding subjects in other namespaces are untouched
